questions.question: What is the normal flow direction and waveform characteristics of the main portal vein (MPV)?
choices: B. Hepatopetal and monophasic with mild respiratory variation
E. Highly resistive with a peak systolic velocity >100 cm/sec
questions.detail: Normal portal flow is toward the liver (hepatopetal) and exhibits a relatively steady, monophasic (phasic) waveform.

questions.question: A pulsatile portal venous waveform is an abnormal finding. What is the most likely etiology?
choices: B. Tricuspid regurgitation or right-sided heart failure
questions.detail: Pulsatility in the portal vein is abnormal and typically reflects transmitted pressure changes from the right heart.

questions.question: In the setting of portal hypertension, what threshold of portal venous flow velocity may mimic thrombosis?
questions.detail: Slow (<16 cm/sec) or stagnant flow is a pitfall that can be mistaken for portal vein thrombosis.

questions.question: "Cavernous transformation" of the portal vein is a sequela of long-standing thrombosis and is characterized by:
choices: A. A single large aneurysmal portal vein
B. Multiple small periportal collateral vessels
C. Reversal of flow in the hepatic artery
D. Air within the portal venous system
E. Thickening of the gallbladder wall
questions.detail: Cavernous transformation consists of numerous tubular collateral vessels at the porta hepatis that bypass the obstructed portal vein.

questions.question: How is portal venous gas distinguished from pneumobilia on ultrasound?
choices: A. Portal gas is central; pneumobilia is peripheral
B. Portal gas extends to the liver periphery; pneumobilia is more central
C. Portal gas is transient; pneumobilia is permanent
D. Pneumobilia causes a "spiky" spectral Doppler waveform
E. There is no sonographic difference
questions.detail: Because of the direction of blood flow, portal venous gas is carried to the periphery, whereas air in the bile ducts (pneumobilia) follows the central distribution of the biliary tree.

questions.question: In a patient with a PATENT transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS), what is the expected flow direction in the right and left portal veins?
choices: D. No flow should be present
questions.detail: In a functioning TIPS, blood from the peripheral portal branches is diverted "backward" toward the shunt.

questions.question: Which cardiac condition is characterized by "accentuated A- and V-waves" on a hepatic vein Doppler tracing?
choices: B. Right-sided heart failure or tricuspid regurgitation
questions.detail: These right-sided abnormalities cause increased retrograde flow during atrial systole, accentuating the waves.

questions.question: Decreased or "flattened" hepatic vein pulsatility is typically seen in which condition?
questions.detail: Narrowing or compression of the hepatic veins (as seen in cirrhosis or outflow obstruction) dampens the normal triphasic pulsatility.
